quote: Oh, I just hear, from Tuesday. She says, 40K w eight.
stewart_read: The customer successfully reads a number off his bill aloud unprompted this early, proving a verbal read-back path was live and working. Instead of leaning into this proven channel, the rep continues chasing a screenshot for another 15 minutes.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged screenshotting was the only viable path since a full year of data was needed and a single day figure wasn't sufficient — but the 12:47 moment shows the customer can also read multi-line breakdowns aloud, undercutting this.
coaching_implication: Train reps to recognize an early successful verbal read-back (04:56) as a signal to pivot fully to read-back for the twelve-month graph, rather than defaulting to screenshot-only once digital friction starts.

quote: Okay. I found that, the the bill the bill breakdown says here, the electric the bill breakdown, bill payment.
stewart_read: Second proof point that verbal read-back works — customer reads multiple line items aloud without issue. The rep still pushes forward with the screenshot/graph hunt for another five minutes rather than asking him to read the twelve bars off the usage graph one by one.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have believed reading twelve months of numbers aloud would take longer than a screenshot — a reasonable time-tradeoff call, but not one the rep tested against the two demonstrated verbal successes.
coaching_implication: Coach the specific pivot point: after two successful verbal reads, offer 'can you just read me the twelve numbers on that graph' as a fallback before continuing screen-navigation guidance.

quote: What is the what is the cost for the paneling?
stewart_read: Customer asks a direct pricing question mid-call. Rep correctly redirects to the specialist rather than answering, which is the right scope discipline.
coaching_implication: This is a positive example — flag it to the rep as the correct move, worth repeating: 'that's actually what my specialist would come over to show you guys.'

quote: I still gotta go with ComEd to, for some for some reason. Right?
stewart_read: Customer asks a substantive net-metering question. Rep admits uncertainty and defers to the specialist rather than guessing, which is the correct knowledge-gap handling.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as good practice: 'I'm not entirely sure, that's something I'll have my specialist go over with you tomorrow' avoids fabrication while keeping the customer engaged.

quote: another company told me that I I'm, you know, the the panelists are free, and they don't have to pay anything, you know. And, you know, another company says, you know, a different story, you know.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a specific, unusual competitor claim (free panels, no cost) that directly conflicts with Ion's model. The rep validates the instinct to compare offers but never asks which company made this claim or notes it for the closer.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged that probing the competitor by name wasn't worth the time this late in a long call — but this is exactly the kind of intel the closer needs to preempt the objection tomorrow.
coaching_implication: There is no dedicated schema section for this exact competitive-disclosure probe; treat it as a coachable gap similar in spirit to rebuttals.already_saw_design (comparison framing) — the rep should have asked 'which company told you that?' and logged it for the closer.
